# Shared Medplum Guidance

## Documentation and Compatibility

- Read the relevant official Medplum documentation once before implementing behavior in an area; prefer documented Medplum patterns over generic FHIR assumptions. Resolve a topic or `[slug]` at `https://www.medplum.com/docs/<slug>`. If an upstream checkout is available, its `packages/docs/docs/` directory contains `.md` and `.mdx` sources; do not assume a checkout, docs skill, or MCP server exists.
- Reuse documentation already read in this session while its actual text remains available. After compaction or loss of that text, re-read the relevant documentation before writing code. These reminders do not replace the docs.
- Follow [root R4, SDK, and security rules](../../AGENTS.md#domain-and-delivery-guidance). Online docs may describe newer features: verify compatibility with the installed SDK and deployed server, including required Project feature flags, rather than silently upgrading or assuming support.

## Domain Guardrails

- **Messaging:** In Medplum's thread model, the header `Communication` has neither `payload` nor `partOf`; child messages carry content and reference the header through `partOf`. The header's `recipient` is the full participant list, including its sender/creator, not just other recipients. See [messaging data model](https://www.medplum.com/docs/communications/messaging-data-model).
- **Scheduling:** With Medplum's implicit-availability model, define recurring availability on the service/schedule; create `Slot` resources only for booked or blocked time, not pre-generated open availability. See [defining availability](https://www.medplum.com/docs/scheduling/defining-availability).
- **Licensure:** For Medplum's service/jurisdiction model, use `PractitionerRole` per service line with jurisdiction `Location` references in `PractitionerRole.location`; multiple states can share a role. Scheduling operations do not enforce licensure. Select eligible schedules and validate eligibility in the controlled booking path, not just the UI; enforce data access separately with `AccessPolicy`. See [state-by-state licensure](https://www.medplum.com/docs/scheduling/state-by-state-licensure).
- **Bundles:** For dependent writes requiring atomicity, use `type: transaction` and matching `urn:uuid` `fullUrl` references for resources created together. Verify transaction support and the required `transaction-bundles` Project flag before relying on rollback; Medplum can otherwise process the bundle as a batch. `reorderBundle()` handles dependency ordering, not atomicity. Use batches only when independent outcomes or explicitly handled partial completion are acceptable. See [FHIR batch requests](https://www.medplum.com/docs/fhir-datastore/fhir-batch-requests).
- **Idempotent writes:** Use supported conditional creates (such as `createResourceIfNoneExist`) or conditional updates keyed on stable identifiers where appropriate; never use search-then-unconditional-create as duplicate prevention. Preserve version-aware update safety and follow the [bot retry/idempotency rules](medplum-bots.instructions.md) for event-driven workflows. See [working with FHIR](https://www.medplum.com/docs/fhir-datastore/working-with-fhir).
- **Files:** Prefer supported SDK upload helpers such as `createBinary`, `createAttachment`, and `createMedia`, with Binary-backed attachment URLs and appropriate `Binary.securityContext`. Avoid embedding full base64 file content in `Attachment.data` unless an explicit interoperability requirement calls for it; it is valid R4, but not Medplum's recommended storage pattern. Do not assume a read returns a literal `Binary/{id}` URL: Medplum can return short-lived signed URLs. See [binary data](https://www.medplum.com/docs/fhir-datastore/binary-data) and [Binary security context](https://www.medplum.com/docs/access/binary-security-context).
- **Access:** Patient-compartment membership depends on each resource's own compartment-defining references (for example `subject`); do not assume access propagates through links such as `Communication.partOf`. Enforce authorization server-side with `AccessPolicy` and `ProjectMembership`; frontend filtering is not a security boundary. Derive UI capabilities from server-backed permissions, including delegated access, rather than equating permission with a project-admin flag. An empty or access-filtered configuration search does not establish that a policy is disabled; distinguish verified policy decisions from missing, unreadable, or invalid configuration. Bind custom policy variables such as `%patient` or `%org` through membership parameters rather than assuming they are built-ins. Validate both allowed and denied access against the server; mocks alone do not prove enforcement. See [access policies](https://www.medplum.com/docs/access/access-policies).
- **Subscriptions:** Scope `criteria` tightly and use documented Medplum extensions when restricting create/update interactions or expressing transitions with `%previous`/`%current`. Account for empty `%previous` on creation and verify extension support on the target server; these are not standard R4 subscription fields. Follow the [bot safety rules](medplum-bots.instructions.md) for loops, retries, and partial effects. See [subscription extensions](https://www.medplum.com/docs/subscriptions/subscription-extensions).
- **Questionnaire extraction:** Prefer SDC `templateExtract`/`$extract` for declarative mappings and a Bot for scoring or complex workflows. Both may process one form when responsibilities are distinct; do not let them duplicate writes to the same targets. Define persistence and retry behavior explicitly: `$extract` returns a Bundle, not persisted resources. See [parsing questionnaire responses](https://www.medplum.com/docs/questionnaires/parsing-questionnaire-responses).
- **Clinical codes:** Never fabricate SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, or other clinical codes or trust arbitrary search results. Verify codes, systems, displays, and versions through authoritative publishers, approved terminology services, or reviewed local value sets. If verification is unavailable, clearly mark the draft placeholder and flag it for human verification; do not ship unverified placeholders to production. Follow terminology stewardship in the hiive-fhir-resources repository for terminology changes. See [common terminologies](https://www.medplum.com/docs/terminology/common-terminologies).

## Clinical Workflow Integrity

- **Flush before signing:** Signing or completing a clinical workflow must persist the latest visible drafts from every participating form. Cancel outstanding debounce timers, await in-flight saves, and persist pending edits before creating the signed note, signature, or completion state. A save failure must prevent a falsely signed or completed chart; define recovery for any partial effects.
- **Define write failure behavior:** Before implementing a write workflow, state its concurrency, retry/idempotency, and partial-failure guarantees. Use supported version checks and stable identities as appropriate; do not suppress a conflict by reading the newest version and blindly overwriting it with a stale clinical draft. Follow the bundle and idempotent-write guardrails above, verify deployed transaction support, and test competing edits, uncertain request outcomes, and failure between dependent writes.
- **Reconcile removed outputs:** Extraction must reconcile added, corrected, removed, and reordered answers with their derived clinical records. Preserve stable answer/output identities and source lineage; do not key record identity solely on editable answer text or array position. Update or retire only outputs owned by that source. Preserve unrelated records and clinical history; signed or finalized records require an appropriate amendment or status-change workflow rather than indiscriminate deletion.

## PHI-Safe Logging

- Do not send raw FHIR resources, questionnaire answers, patient identifiers, reference `display` strings, tokens, or secrets to console output, application logs, analytics, or error-reporting services. URLs, search criteria, signed attachment URLs, and `OperationOutcome` diagnostics can also contain sensitive data. Prefer allowlisted diagnostic fields such as operation name, resource type, and status code; reuse existing redaction utilities rather than assuming an error object is safe. When changing logging or error handling, test that sensitive fields and secrets are omitted or redacted.
- Diagnostic logging is not a replacement for a protected audit trail. Verify which actions the deployed server already audits before adding custom `AuditEvent` writes; do not blindly duplicate events per request or introduce fallback stores for sensitive data. Any additional audit workflow needs explicit access, retention, and failure-handling decisions. Bot console output can be persisted in audit events; tutorial logging examples are not permission to log PHI. See [Bot Basics](https://www.medplum.com/docs/bots/bot-basics).

## Testing Procedures

- Reuse the owning workspace's test runner, setup, fixtures, and helpers. Use only synthetic data, isolate `MockClient` state between tests, and await asynchronous setup and assertions. Mocks exercise application logic, not deployed-server guarantees.
- For bug fixes, first reproduce the reported behavior with a focused regression test that fails before the repair and passes afterward. Exercise relevant failure and lifecycle cases, including immediate edit-then-sign, encounter switches or unmounts with pending work, answer correction/removal/reordering, retries, authentication versus transport failures, concurrent writers, and partial persistence. Use focused application tests plus authorized server-backed checks for server permission or concurrency guarantees; obtain explicit authorization for live checks that mutate data and use only a disposable environment with synthetic accounts and fixtures.
- Distinguish local `validateResource` from `@medplum/core` (returns `OperationOutcomeIssue[]` when it returns normally, but throws `OperationOutcomeError` for invalid resources in the installed SDK) from `medplum.validateResource` / server `$validate` (returns an `OperationOutcome`, with request failures potentially throwing). Local validation requires loaded R4 definitions; reuse the FHIR test setup in the hiive-fhir-resources repository where applicable. For a custom profile, load its generated snapshot and supply it through the installed validator's supported profile option; creating a `StructureDefinition` in a mock store alone does not configure local validation. Test valid and invalid resources and inspect outcome issue codes and expressions, including on thrown errors. Do not report local validation as proof of server enforcement or complete terminology validation.
- `deepEquals` ignores `meta.versionId` and `meta.lastUpdated` in the installed SDK. Assert these fields explicitly when testing version-aware writes or concurrency; use focused assertions for business fields and reference integrity rather than relying solely on whole-resource equality.

## Completion Checks

- Re-check the applicable guardrails before finishing. Run the owning workspace's existing build/typecheck, focused tests, and required [root validation gate](../../AGENTS.md#development-commands) for code or resource changes. Compile FSH through SUSHI and inspect generated artifacts when FSH changes; do not invent validation commands for the uninitialized bot workspace.
